evidence: Suet. Aug. 57.2: prō facultāte quisque pecūniās contulērunt, each gave money as he could afford
Liv. 26.36: in pūblicum cōnferāmus, let us give it to the treasury
terms.comment: The gift in the accusative, the cause after in or ad: pecūniam in rem cōnferre. A small coin given is a stips (see alms).

evidence: Hor. S. 1.5.65–66: dōnāsset jamne catēnam ex vōtō Laribus, whether he had yet given his chain to the household gods, as he had vowed
terms.comment: To give as a present (see give), to a person or to the gods.

phrases.latin: In restitūtiōnem Palātīnae domūs incendiō absūmptae veterānī, decuriae, tribūs atque etiam singillātim ē cēterō genere hominum libentēs ac prō facultāte quisque pecūniās contulērunt
phrases.english: For the rebuilding of his house on the Palatine, which had burned down, the veterans, the guilds, the tribes and individuals of every other sort gave money, gladly and each as he could afford

sources: Lewis & Short: confero · Lewis & Short: dono
